evidence: src/domain/order-service.ts: `private reservations: Map<string, StockReservation[]> = new Map();` keeps reservation records keyed by orderId across calls.
src/domain/order-service.ts reserveStock: `this.reservations.set(orderId, validItems);` saves reservation records.
src/domain/order-service.ts getReservedItems / releaseReservations: `this.reservations.get(orderId)` and `this.reservations.delete(orderId)` are repository-style read and delete operations.

Graph: PlaceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and TransitionOrderUseCase all receive OrderDomainService through their constructors, and src/infrastructure/server.ts imports it. The stored state is therefore shared between use cases and requests.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Most of OrderDomainService is proper domain logic. canTransition and validateTransition enforce the order state machine, and reserveStock decides whether all items can be reserved, with the stock lookup passed in as a callback. The problem is that the class also stores reservation state. The private field `reservations: Map<string, StockReservation[]>` holds data keyed by orderId across calls. reserveStock saves it with set, getReservedItems reads it with get, and releaseReservations and clearReservations remove it with delete. The graph shows that PlaceOrderUseCase, CancelOrderUseCase and TransitionOrderUseCase all receive this service through their constructors, and server.ts in the infrastructure layer imports it. That means the reservations live in a single shared instance between requests, so the service is acting as an in-memory repository for StockReservation records. Storing and retrieving records by key is a persistence job. It belongs in a repository whose interface lives in the domain or application layer and whose implementation lives in infrastructure. A domain service should not do it. Because no I/O is involved this is a judgement call, hence the moderate confidence.

violations.message: OrderDomainService stores, reads and deletes StockReservation records through its private Map `reservations` (reserveStock -> set, getReservedItems/releaseReservations -> get/delete), so it works as an in-memory repository. Storing records like this is a persistence (infrastructure) job. It should sit behind a repository interface with the implementation in infrastructure, and the domain service should not hold state.
